memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Visit for review of vertigo, IBS and anxiety.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports episodic spinning sensation lasting seconds, triggered by head movements; abdominal bloating and occasional diarrhea; worry and tension most days.
EXAMINATION: General: alert, oriented. BP 138/86 mmHg, weight 68 kg, BMI 28.3 (obese). Advise diet low in salt, regular walking 30 minutes daily. ENT: Dix-Hallpike test pending. Abdomen: soft, non-tender. Neuro: normal.
IMPRESSION: 1. Benign positional vertigo, likely posterior canalithiasis. 2. Irritable bowel syndrome, diarrhoea-predominant. 3. Generalised anxiety disorder, moderate. Annual fasting lipid profile and fasting blood sugar ordered.
ARRANGEMENTS: Start betahistine 16 mg BD, meclizine 25 mg SOS for vertigo; mebeverine 135 mg BD, ispaghula husk 5 g OD, loperamide 2 mg SOS for IBS; escitalopram 5 mg OD, buspirone 5 mg BD for anxiety. Review in 3 months. Return if: sudden severe vertigo with vomiting, black/tarry stools, fever >39°C, chest pain, or worsening anxiety with panic attacks.

memories.author: D03

Loperamide 2 mg as needed

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
Fasting lipid profile: Total cholesterol 5.2 mmol/L (<5.2 normal), LDL 3.4 mmol/L (<2.6 high), HDL 1.2 mmol/L (>1.0 normal), Triglycerides 1.8 mmol/L (<1.7 borderline).
Fasting blood sugar: 6.1 mmol/L (3.9-5.5 normal, prediabetes).

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Dix-Hallpike test: Positive for posterior canal BPPV on the right side; torsional upbeat nystagmus observed.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Audiometry (pure tone average): Right ear 25 dB HL, Left ear 22 dB HL; bilateral mild high-frequency loss, consistent with age-related changes.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: Vertigo episodes have decreased to about twice a week, less severe. Bloating better with ispaghula husk. Still feel anxious most days, but sleeping improved.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Follow-up for vertigo, IBS and anxiety.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Vertigo now occasional, mild; abdominal discomfort with loose stools twice weekly; reports persistent worry and muscle tension.
EXAMINATION: BP 134/82 mmHg, weight 67 kg, BMI 27.9 (obese). Advise reduce refined carbs, add yoga twice weekly. ENT: symptom‑guided Dix‑Hallpike negative today. Abdomen: mild tenderness in left lower quadrant, no masses. Neuro: normal.
IMPRESSION: 1. Improving benign positional vertigo. 2. IBS with mixed pattern, likely exacerbated by stress. 3. Generalised anxiety disorder, moderate‑severe. Lipids and FBS from April show borderline high LDL and prediabetes; will repeat in January.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue betahistine 16 mg BD; stop meclizine SOS (no longer needed). Increase mebeverine to 135 mg TDS; continue ispaghula husk 5 g OD; add loperamide 2 mg SOS only for diarrhoea. Escitalopram increase to 10 mg OD; buspirone continue 5 mg BD. Review in 3 months. Return if: vertigo with falling, blood in stool, weight loss >3 kg, fever >39°C, or panic attacks with chest pain.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Betahistine 16 mg twice daily
Mebeverine 135 mg three times daily
Ispaghula husk 5 g once daily
Loperamide 2 mg as needed
Escitalopram 10 mg once daily
Buspirone 5 mg twice daily

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
Complete blood count: Hb 12.8 g/L (12-16 normal), WBC 6.2 x10^9/L (4-10 normal), Platelets 210 x10^9/L (150-400 normal).
Stool routine: Ova and parasites nil, pus cells 0-2/hpf.
tTG‑IgA: <4 U/mL (<7 negative).

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Autumn review of vertigo, IBS and anxiety; influenza vaccination.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Vertigo rare, only with rapid head turns; IBS symptoms controlled with occasional loperamide; anxiety improved but still reports tension.
EXAMINATION: BP 130/80 mmHg, weight 66 kg, BMI 27.4 (obese). Advise maintain Mediterranean diet, daily 30‑min walk. ENT: Dix‑Hallpike negative. Abdomen: soft, non‑tender. Neuro: normal.
IMPRESSION: 1. Benign positional vertigo, well controlled. 2. Irritable bowel syndrome, mild. 3. Generalised anxiety disorder, improving. Annual lipids and FBS due in January.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue betahistine 16 mg BD; mebeverine 135 mg BD; ispaghula husk 5 g OD; loperamide 2 mg SOS. Escitalopram 10 mg OD; buspirone 5 mg BD. Influenza vaccine (0.5 mL IM) given today. Review in 3 months. Return if: vertigo with falls, severe abdominal pain, bleeding per rectum, fever >39°C, or worsening anxiety with suicidal thoughts.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Appointment booked for 2026-01-20 at 10:30 AM with Dr Priya Natarajan (D03) for routine follow‑up.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Winter follow‑up for vertigo, IBS and anxiety; repeat metabolic screening.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: No vertigo episodes in past 2 months; IBS symptoms minimal, occasional bloating; anxiety well controlled, occasional worry.
EXAMINATION: BP 128/78 mmHg, weight 65 kg, BMI 27.0 (obese). Advise continue balanced diet, light resistance training twice weekly. ENT: Dix‑Hallpike negative. Abdomen: soft, non‑tender. Neuro: normal.
IMPRESSION: 1. Benign positional vertigo, resolved. 2. Irritable bowel syndrome, in remission. 3. Generalised anxiety disorder, mild. Fasting lipid profile: total cholesterol 4.9 mmol/L, LDL 2.8 mmol/L, HDL 1.3 mmol/L, triglycerides 1.5 mmol/L. Fasting blood sugar: 5.6 mmol/L (prediabetes range).
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue betahistine 16 mg BD; mebeverine 135 mg BD; ispaghula husk 5 g OD; loperamide 2 mg SOS. Escitalopram 10 mg OD; buspirone 5 mg BD. Review in 6 months. Return if: vertigo returns, severe abdominal pain, weight loss >4 kg, fever >39°C, or worsening anxiety with panic attacks.
